note: DRAFT fixture payload for trusted builder registration as art-741. Every `output_payload` here was produced by executing the ported kernel, AND independently matched field-for-field against the Apex page's own compute, extracted verbatim from the pinned snapshot and run under Node (provenance/apex-reference.mjs). `apex_output_payload` is the page's own answer; `output_payload` is the kernel's; they are compared on 32 numeric/boolean fields plus the 10 strings the page renders and the 5 AP2 export values, strictly, with no tolerance. Boundary fixtures come in `:at` / `:past` pairs, one pair per comparator in the page's compute.

comparators.name: B17-total-hours-worked-division-guard
comparators.note: The guard the prior run (APEXPORT-132) could not make flip. Re-derived from the page: totalHoursWorked = travelHours x weeksWorked = travelHours x contractWeeks x contractsPerYear, and 0 on any of those three factors is swallowed by the `|| default` guards, which substitute 36 / 13 / 3. So the guard's exact zero crossing is UNREACHABLE and the reachable flip is a sign boundary: a negative travelHours drives totalHoursWorked below 0, the guard fires, and effectiveHourly returns the literal 0 instead of dividing. Past zero -- i.e. positive -- the division happens and effectiveHourly becomes travelNetAnnual / 39.

comparators.name: B18-division-guard-zero-is-unreachable
comparators.note: Proof by fixture, not by assertion: travelHours = 0 and travelHours = 36 produce a BYTE-IDENTICAL output_payload on the page, because 0 is falsy and reverts to the default 36. The same holds for contractWeeks (0 reverts to 13) and contractsPerYear (0 reverts to 3). Therefore the divide-by-zero the guard was written for cannot be reached through the page's inputs at all. Cross-check: travelHours = 1 divides and yields a different effectiveHourly, so the guard is live, just not at zero.
